beats.text: People chose more pain over less. Voluntarily.
In a classic experiment, people held one hand in painfully cold water for sixty seconds.
The other hand got the same sixty seconds. Plus thirty more, while the water got slightly warmer.
Memory doesn't add up the minutes. It keeps the worst moment and the ending. The peak end rule.
So want a good memory? Give it a good ending.

sources: Kahneman, Fredrickson, Schreiber & Redelmeier (1993). When more pain is preferred to less: Adding a better end. Psychological Science 4(6), 401-405. Short trial: 60 s at 14 °C; long trial: 60 s at 14 °C + 30 s while warming to ~15 °C. 22 of 32 (69%) chose to repeat the long trial; replication 24 of 37.
